questions.text: Which set best describes the usual areas covered by IT general controls (ITGCs)?

options.A: Preventive, detective and corrective controls over financial reporting
options.B: Revenue, purchasing, payroll and treasury cycles across all business units
options.C: Access to programs and data, program changes, development and IT operations
options.D: Input, processing and output checks built into a single application

questions.explanation: ITGCs cover access, change, development and IT operations across systems; input/processing/output controls are application controls.

questions.text: An auditor finds that several employees who left the company months ago still have active accounts in the finance application. Which control would best address this risk?

options.A: Encrypt the finance database and restrict who holds the encryption keys
options.B: Require formal approval and testing before any change goes live
options.C: Review the password policy each year and enforce much stronger complexity rules
options.D: Remove access promptly on HR leaver notice, backed by periodic access reviews

questions.explanation: Timely de-provisioning driven by HR leaver notifications, plus periodic reviews to catch misses, directly targets leavers' access.

questions.text: A developer can move their own code changes into the production environment. What is the main risk?

options.A: System performance may drop during busy processing periods
options.B: Nightly backups may fail if production changes too often
options.C: Unreviewed or untested changes can reach production
options.D: Software licences may be exceeded as more users are added

questions.explanation: Developing and migrating to production are incompatible duties; combining them lets changes bypass independent approval.

questions.text: In an audit finding structured as condition, criteria, cause and effect, what does "criteria" mean?

options.A: The underlying reason the issue was able to happen
options.B: The policy or standard the condition is measured against
options.C: The facts the auditor actually observed during testing
options.D: The actual or potential impact of the issue on the business

questions.explanation: Condition is "what is"; criteria is "what should be".

questions.text: Under the IIA Three Lines Model, who provides independent assurance to the governing body?

options.A: Operational management
options.B: Internal audit
options.C: Risk management and compliance functions
options.D: External regulators

questions.explanation: Internal audit is the third line. Regulators and external auditors sit outside the three lines.

questions.text: Which sampling method gives every item in the population an equal, known chance of being selected?

options.A: Judgmental sampling
options.B: Haphazard sampling
options.C: Random sampling
options.D: Block sampling

questions.explanation: Random selection gives each item an equal chance. Haphazard sampling avoids deliberate bias but isn't truly random.

questions.text: Which of these is an application control?

options.A: A system three-way match of order, receipt and invoice before payment
options.B: A change advisory board that approves all ERP changes each week
options.C: A nightly backup of the ERP database copied to a second data centre
options.D: A quarterly review of all ERP user accounts by the IT security team

questions.explanation: The three-way match is built into the purchasing process of one application; the others are IT general controls.

questions.text: What is the main objective of change management controls?

options.A: A complete list of software licences is kept up to date
options.B: Users can adjust their own access when their role changes
options.C: Only authorised, tested and approved changes reach production
options.D: Changes reach production as quickly as the business requests them

questions.explanation: Change management ensures production changes are authorised, tested and approved before release.

questions.text: In backup and disaster recovery, what does the recovery point objective (RPO) define?

options.A: The maximum acceptable downtime after a disruption
options.B: The maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time
options.C: The distance required between primary and backup sites
options.D: The number of backup copies that must be retained

questions.explanation: RPO is how much data (time since the last good copy) can be lost; RTO is how long systems can be down.

questions.text: How many components does the COSO Internal Control – Integrated Framework (2013) have?

options.A: Three
options.B: Eight
options.C: Seventeen
options.D: Five

questions.explanation: Five components: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, monitoring activities (supported by 17 principles).

questions.text: What is ISO/IEC 27001 mainly?

options.A: A framework for the governance and management of enterprise IT
options.B: A certifiable standard for an information security management system
options.C: A professional standard for the audit of annual financial statements
options.D: An internal control framework for reliable financial reporting

questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 sets the requirements for an ISMS and organisations can be certified against it; COBIT and COSO are the other frameworks described.

questions.text: What are the three elements of the fraud triangle?

options.A: Planning, fieldwork and reporting
options.B: Prevention, detection and incident response
options.C: Motive, means and method
options.D: Pressure, opportunity and rationalisation

questions.explanation: Fraud is more likely when someone feels pressure, has the opportunity, and can rationalise the act.

questions.text: Four IT staff share the password of one generic administrator account on the ERP system. What is the main risk?

options.A: Scheduled backups may fail to run overnight
options.B: The ERP may run out of named user licences
options.C: The shared password may expire too often
options.D: Actions can't be traced to one person

questions.explanation: Shared privileged accounts remove individual accountability, so misuse can't be attributed to a person.

questions.text: Which audit evidence is generally the most reliable?

options.A: A scanned copy of an invoice emailed to the auditor by the auditee
options.B: A confirmation sent directly to the auditor by a third party
options.C: A detailed verbal explanation given by the finance manager
options.D: A spreadsheet prepared internally by the auditee's own team

questions.explanation: Evidence from independent external sources, obtained directly by the auditor, is generally more reliable than internal or oral evidence.

questions.text: An auditor tests 25 change tickets and finds 3 changes deployed without approval. What is the best next step?

options.A: Replace the 3 exceptions with new items from the population
options.B: Accept the result, since 88% of the sample was approved
options.C: Stop the audit and report that all change controls failed
options.D: Find the cause, check the 3 changes and report the exceptions

questions.explanation: Exceptions must be followed up and reported, not replaced or ignored; understanding the cause and impact shapes the finding.

questions.text: In an audit finding, what does the "cause" explain?

options.A: Why the condition happened
options.B: What the policy requires
options.C: What the auditor observed
options.D: The impact on the organisation

questions.explanation: The cause is the underlying reason for the gap between condition and criteria; recommendations should target it.

questions.text: In the system development life cycle (SDLC), when should security requirements ideally be defined?

options.A: During the requirements and design phases
options.B: After go-live, during the first internal audit
options.C: Only during user acceptance testing
options.D: When the system is retired

questions.explanation: Building security in from requirements and design is cheaper and more effective than adding it later.

questions.text: The monthly user access review for the payroll system is performed by the IT administrator who also grants the access. What is the main weakness?

options.A: The review should cover all company systems at the same time
options.B: Monthly reviews are more frequent than is necessary
options.C: The reviewer is checking access they granted themselves
options.D: Payroll access doesn't need to be reviewed at all

questions.explanation: Reviews should be done by business owners independent of the person granting access; otherwise the reviewer checks their own work.

questions.text: What is inherent risk?

options.A: The risk before considering the effect of controls
options.B: The risk left after controls are applied
options.C: The risk that the auditor fails to detect an error
options.D: The risk the organisation is willing to accept

questions.explanation: Inherent risk exists before controls; residual risk remains after them.

questions.text: A small company cannot separate the person who records cash receipts from the person who deposits them. Which is the best compensating control?

options.A: An independent monthly review of the bank reconciliations
options.B: Asking the employee to sign the code of conduct each year
options.C: Rotating the employee to a different desk each quarter
options.D: Raising the employee's pay to reduce any financial pressure

questions.explanation: An independent review of reconciliations would detect receipts that were recorded but not deposited (or vice versa), compensating for the missing segregation.
